hero: In a freestanding hemodialysis unit in Caloocan, a Filipina nephrology fellow holds up a can of luncheon meat and points to its ingredient list while a middle-aged Filipino patient in a dialysis chair and his wife lean in to read; dialysis machines and morning light in the background, encouraging mood, no text.

figures.teaches: In CKD, FGF23 rises first and serum phosphate rises last, so a normal phosphate does not mean a normal mineral axis.
figures.content: Left organ panel: kidney with fewer nephrons labeled 'Nephron loss'. Bone icon releasing 'FGF23 rises (first)'. Kidney inset with 'Klotho falls' and 'Calcitriol falls'. Gut panel 'Less calcium absorbed'. Parathyroid glands enlarging 'PTH rises'. Bone panel 'High turnover: bone pain, fractures'. Artery cross-section with calcium deposits 'Phosphate rises (late): vascular and valve calcification'. Timeline bar across bottom: 'CKD G2-G3: FGF23 up' -> 'G3-G4: PTH up' -> 'G4-G5: phosphate up'. Footnote: 'CRIC cohort, 3,879 adults, CKD stages 2-4'.

figures.teaches: Phosphate additives in processed foods are absorbed far more completely than phosphate in plant foods, and patients can find them on labels.
figures.content: Left: mock ingredient list of a canned luncheon meat with 'sodium tripolyphosphate' and 'sodium phosphate' circled, heading 'Look for PHOS'. Right: three stacked bars labeled 'Plant foods (phytate): absorbed least', 'Meat, fish, dairy: absorbed more', 'Inorganic additives: absorbed most'. Bottom row of Filipino foods with swap arrows: 'Hotdog, longganisa, luncheon meat -> fresh fish or chicken', 'Instant noodles -> rice with vegetables', 'Cola -> water within fluid allowance'. Footer: 'Education on additives lowered phosphate by 0.6 mg/dL more over 3 months (RCT, 279 patients)'.

card: A hand holding a canned processed meat with a magnifying glass over the ingredient list, beside a plate of rice and fresh fish, no text.
